_help: Optional prose rendered on the site. Each section takes 'simple' (plain language, default view) and 'advanced' text; Markdown subset: blank line = new paragraph, **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [link](https://…). Empty strings are ignored. luna.best: run label, display name or variant id to highlight as the configuration confirmed on the test split (otherwise the export's 'confirmed' flag is used). luna.takeaway: replaces the auto-generated Luna takeaway in the simple view.

formats.simple: We tested GPT-6 Luna in four kinds of games: **cash games** (deep stacks), **tournaments** at 40 and 20 big blinds, and **Spin & Go** (very short stacks). After the flop, Luna loses the most in deep cash games, where pots get big and mistakes are expensive, and the least in short-stacked games. Before the flop it is the other way round: it plays deep stacks fine but used to be its worst with short stacks — until we told it one sentence about short-stack strategy (see Part 4).
formats.advanced: Postflop numbers come from full-hand suites (flop solves from preflop ranges, every decision of both seats on flop/turn/river, no triviality filter); preflop numbers from heads-up preflop suites (exact push/fold Nash ≤12bb, equity-realisation tree deeper). Tournament formats are chip EV — ICM is not modelled. bb/100 lost = Σ EV loss per hand ÷ 2 seats, 95% CI over hands; it is dominated by a few large-pot mistakes, so EV loss in % pot is the steadier per-decision metric.

arena.simple: Here the models played **whole hands** against two computer opponents: a solid 'regular' (TAG bot) and a 'calling station' that never folds. **No model beat the solid regular** — GPT-6 Luna broke even and Mercury came close. Against the calling station every model won, and most won *more* than the solid bot does, because they bet a lot and that is exactly how you beat someone who never folds. Luna was the exception: careful and balanced, it barely exploited the weak player.
arena.advanced: Duplicate format (each deal played twice with seats swapped), 100bb, blinds 0.5/1. Models were run with the default state (pre-optimisation). bb/100 CIs are wide at 300–500 hands; the TAG bot's own +242 bb/100 vs the station is the reference.

luna.simple:
We tried many ways of describing the same poker spot to GPT-6 Luna and kept only what improved it on hands it had **never seen** (a separate test set). Two changes stood out:

After the flop, telling Luna **how close its hand is to the best possible hand** (and its chance to win against the hands the opponent is likely to hold) cut its mistakes by about **30%** in cash games and **30–40%** in tournaments and Spin & Go.

Before the flop with short stacks, **one sentence of standard short-stack advice** ("limp, fold or go all-in; small raises are rarely right") roughly **halved** its losses in Spin & Go. Without it, Luna never went all-in preflop.

Things that did *not* help: theory-heavy coaching, asking the same question three ways, yes/no questions per action, and giving less information. Even improved, Luna still loses to perfect play — just much less.
luna.advanced: Protocol: variants tuned on the cash dev split (337 decisions), confirmed on the held-out test split (324 decisions) and then on independent MTT 40bb / MTT 20bb / Spin full-hand suites and two independent Spin preflop suites. Postflop winner `nuts` = `eqrange` (Monte-Carlo equity vs the villain's preflop range narrowed by its actions with a strength heuristic — no solver data) + exact nut ranking (number of villain holdings that beat hero now) + one sentence on value extraction with strong hands. Test split: EV loss 2.19% → 1.52% pot (paired Δ −0.67 ± 0.65%, significant), bb/100 lost 179 → 142. MTT40 89 → 55, MTT20 56 → 40, Spin 46 → 28 bb/100 lost (all paired-significant). Preflop winner `shortstack` (≤30bb: v2 + one sentence of short-stack guidance): Spin preflop score 75.7 → 87.2 and 71.0 → 84.6 on an independent suite; MTT20 71.4 → 84.0 (all significant). Equity facts *hurt* preflop (eq/coach significantly worse than v2). Sharpening Luna's distribution (τ = 4) makes its mixed strategy nearly as good as its argmax (cash test 3.36% → 2.36% pot). Ensembles of Luna variants and `multi`/`noul` gave no reliable gain; the fold guardrail never triggered. Recommended configuration: **`nuts` postflop + `shortstack` preflop (v2 preflop when deeper than 30bb)**.
luna.takeaway: Two small, legitimate additions made GPT-6 Luna much better: telling it how close its hand is to the nuts (≈30–40% fewer postflop losses) and one sentence of short-stack advice (≈half the preflop losses in Spin & Go).
